speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly when you first noticed the double vision, and whether your difficulty climbing stairs or upper limb weakness has progressed steadily over time. To help narrow this down, do you have any history of thyroid disease, recent viral infections, or muscle fatigue that worsens with activity and improves with rest?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with diplopia triggered by looking up or down, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receiver_Antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation. Do you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking clearly?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation
